It's a predictable consequence of our most commonly used voting system. I advocate for switching to Approval Voting. Will approval voting give third parties a fighting chance to win? Probably not, but because it gives voters a risk-free way to support their favorite candidate, no matter how fringe, it will cause elections to accurately report third-party support. A candidate that 30% of voters support will be listened to whether they win or not. A candidate with 1% won't, even if they have a survey saying 30% of likely voters prefer them to the guy who won.

The primary drawback of approval voting is the large transitional costs. All ballot templates which include instructions like "Vote for ONE" will need to be amended to read "Vote for ONE or MORE". Additionally, all vote counting software will need to have the subroutine that voids overvoted ballots commented out.
